title: South Sudan: Authorities must protect civic space ahead of scheduled national elections
content:
Following the announced dissolution of South Sudan’s Revitalized Transitional Government of National Unity, a decisive step towards the country’s first-ever elections scheduled for 22 December, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for East and Southern Africa, Tigere Chagutah, said:

“Ahead of these long-awaited and historic elections, South Sudanese authorities must ensure that a conducive environment exists for people to vote and stand in elections, including respect for and enjoyment of human rights, and freedom from discrimination and arbitrary or unnecessary and disproportionate restrictions.

“The legitimacy of any election depends not only on whether it is held, but on whether people can exercise their rights freely, safely and equally. For years, Amnesty International and other organizations have documented the repressive tactics deployed by the South Sudanese authorities to silence dissent, detain critics, and restrict freedom of expression and the right to protest.

title: Europe: Israel’s participation in the UEFA Nations League is a betrayal of Palestinians, football’s own rules and human rights
content:
Ahead of the opening matches of the 2026/27 men’s UEFA Nations League group phase where Austria, Ireland and Kosovo will play against Israel during the 24 September – 6 October international window, Steve Cockburn, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for Europe said: 

“It’s unconscionable that the Israel men’s football team will participate in the UEFA Nations League this autumn despite clear evidence that Israel’s football association continues to support illegal settlements.

“Instead of sending a clear message that there is a cost for Israel’s unlawful occupation of the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT) and its atrocity crimes against Palestinians, UEFA is giving Israel an international stage as it maintains its brutal occupation of the OPT, its system of apartheid over all Palestinians, and its ongoing genocide against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip.

title: Türkiye’s crackdown on LGBTI groups and activists is part of an escalating rights crisis
content:
On 13 September, I woke in southwest Türkiye to news of a large-scale operation targeting LGBTI organizations and human rights defenders across the country. Since then, police have arrested at least 116 people across 15 provinces following raids on homes, venues and the offices of LGBTI rights organizations. At least 83 people have been placed in pretrial detention and criminal investigations have been launched against more than 160 people. LGBTI rights organisations have reported allegations of intrusive strip searches, insults and humiliation as well as HRDs being held in isolation in violation of their rights. Hundreds of social media accounts belonging to LGBTI organizations and activists, journalists, media outlets and others have so far been blocked or restricted alongside a number of websites. Those affected include Amnesty International Türkiye’s X account.  

As protest within Türkiye builds and international condemnation mounts, it is clear that the Turkish authorities have every intention of intensifying the crackdown

Milena Buyum, Amnesty International

title: Pakistan: Arbitrary detention of Imran Khan’s family and party activists a flagrant violation of human rights
content:
Responding to the arbitrary detention of members of former prime minister Imran Khan’s family, including his three sisters, as well as activists from Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) ahead of the party’s planned protests and march on 27 September , Babu Ram Pant, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for South Asia, said: 

“The targeting of Imran Khan’s family and PTI party activists is a flagrant violation of their rights to liberty, freedom of expression, association and peaceful assembly. Such actions speak to the severity of the current restrictions in Pakistan. 

“The pre-emptive arrests of PTI members come ahead of planned country-wide protests by the party on 27 September, which government officials have openly vowed to stop. Roadblocks are already being erected in Islamabad. These developments do not bode well, especially given the authorities’ long track record of reckless and unlawful use of force against protesters. A protest cannot be deemed violent before it has even started. Pakistan’s authorities must uphold their obligations under international human rights law to facilitate peaceful assembly and refrain from unlawful measures to thwart these protests.

title: An artisanal miner on torture and ill treatment by Rwanda Backed M23 fighters
content: In eastern DRC, Rwanda-backed March 23 Movement (M23) fighters have committed horrific human rights abuses against artisanal miners while facilitating the trafficking of gold and coltan to neighbouring Rwanda with the help of Rwandan authorities. The miners recount horrific encounters with the fighters which include summary killings; torture and ill-treatment; arbitrary detention; forced labour and forced recruitment. In this interview one of the miners tells Amnesty International of his ordeal in a mine shaft in the hands of the M23 fighters. From daily beatings to being left inside the shafts for hours and being denied his rightful wages. This is his story which is replicated across the mines.

title: Venezuela: Civil Society Organizations call for the renewal of Key UN Fact-Finding Mission
content:
In a joint statement published today, a group of 21 civil society organizations, including Amnesty International, call for the renewal of the UN Fact-Finding Mission on Venezuela (FFM) and address key questions regarding this special UN mechanism, including what the FFM is and why must it be maintained at least until 2028; how the FFM is complementary to the work of the UN Human Rights Office and international justice mechanisms; and, crucially, how the mission can contribute to the future of Venezuela.

This statement follows an interactive dialogue held at the UN Human Rights Council (HRC) in Geneva on 18 September 2026, during its ongoing 63rd session, where the FFM presented its most recent findings, and several civil society organizations issued oral statements calling on the Council to renew the FFM’s mandate for another two years.

title: Global: Amid mounting threats, the UN’s next Secretary-General must be a staunch defender of international law
content:
Amnesty International’s Secretary General Agnès Callamard will be in New York City for the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly from September 22 to 26 and available for interviews. She will be meeting with senior UN figures and focusing her visit on the following issues:

  • The selection of the next UN Secretary-General, and the state of the UN, multilateralism and the rules-based order
  • Artificial Intelligence and the need for a global, binding, transparent, and effective regulatory model
  • The Trump administration’s continuing attacks on international justice institutions
  • International and multilateral responses to Israel’s genocide in Gaza and ethnic cleansing in the West Bank
  • US-Israeli unlawful attacks on Iran, violations of international law and war crimes
  • Iran’s internal repression, including crimes against humanity
  • Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine
  • Sudan, the role of the UAE and the international community
  • DRC, critical minerals and Rwanda

title: Pakistan: Re-arrest of Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha is a terrible injustice
content:
Reacting to the re-arrest of human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha just hours after they had been granted bail by the Supreme Court yesterday, Babu Ram Pant, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for South Asia, said:

“Imaan and Hadi’s re-arrest dispels any pretence that the charges against them are anything other than a politically motivated attempt to punish them for their human rights work. Their case demonstrates once again the authorities’ willingness to weaponize the legal system against critical voices.

“These latest charges, brought against them for simply attending a peaceful protest, are not only absurd but an insult to their lifelong commitment to human rights.

Their case demonstrates once again the authorities’ willingness to weaponize the legal system against critical voices

title: Philippines: Authorities must ensure right to protest as fresh anti-corruption demonstrations planned
content:
Ahead of planned demonstrations marking one year since mass anti-corruption protests took place in the Philippines on 21 September 2025, Ritz Lee Santos III, Executive Director of Amnesty International Philippines, said:

“As people prepare to take to the streets once more to demand accountability for corruption, Philippine authorities must ensure the right to peaceful assembly is protected and refrain from using excessive force. The authorities must not repeat the mistakes of last year’s violent response to peaceful protest.

“One year on, protesters arrested during the 2025 demonstrations continue to face charges, while authorities have failed to thoroughly, independently and impartially investigate allegations of police violence.

“Charges against those who exercised their right to peaceful assembly should be immediately dropped. Any use of force by police must be strictly necessary, proportionate and in line with international human rights standards.

title: US State Department must reverse decision to ban Palestine delegation from attending UNGA session in New York
content:
Responding to the US State Department’s announcement in a statement yesterday that it has, for the second consecutive year, barred the high-level delegation of the State of Palestine, including Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas, from attending the UN General Assembly in New York, Amnesty International’s Senior Director for Research, Policy, Advocacy and Campaigns, Erika Guevara Rosas said: 

“The decision by the US State Department to deny visas to a high-level delegation of the State of Palestine to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly must be reversed. The State Department’s statement makes it obvious: this decision is designed to punish the State of Palestine for pursuing international justice and accountability at international institutions, including through the International Criminal Court (ICC) and International Court of Justice (ICJ). This measure is part of a relentless campaign of reprisals against the very notion of international justice. 

This measure is part of a relentless campaign of reprisals against the very notion of international justice. 

Erika Guevara Rosas, Amnesty International

title: Global: Women Human Rights Defenders take their fight to the UN during week-long advocacy meeting
content:
Women Human Right Defenders (WHRDs) from around the world will be gathering in Geneva from 21 to 25 September, to learn about the UN Human Rights Council, advocate for their rights and amplify their own stories.

The week-long training, known as the Women Human Rights Advocacy Week, is co-organized by nine human rights organizations including Amnesty International (see below for full list). It is aimed at providing participants with practical tools to understand the Human Rights Council, while offering guidance on how to engage with it strategically and advocate for change in their communities.

“The women attending are risking their lives every day to protect their communities from climate change, greedy corporations and land theft,” said Lisa Maracani, Amnesty International’s researcher on human rights defenders. “Their knowledge is crucial to ensuring bodies such as the Human Rights Council remain effective, while the WHRD Advocacy Week is designed to provide these women with the tools and strategies to advance their advocacy on this global stage.”

title: Kosovo: War crimes convictions of former president ‘shows senior officials are not above the law’
content:
Reacting to the convictions for war crimes of Hashim Thaçi, Kadri Veseli, Rexhep Selimi and Jakup Krasniqi by the Kosovo Specialist Chamber, Esther Major, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for Europe, said: 

These verdicts give hope that the victims and relatives of the missing will finally see justice

Esther Major, Amnesty International

These verdicts give hope that the victims and relatives of the missing will finally see justice

“These convictions give hope to thousands of victims of the Kosovo war who have waited for more than two decades to get justice for the horrific crimes committed against them and to know the fate of their loved ones.  

“These convictions show that senior officials are not above the law. 

“These verdicts give hope that any attempt to obstruct justice, truth and reparation will not be tolerated, and that the victims and relatives of the missing will finally see justice.” 

Background

The Trial Panel of the Kosovo Specialist Chamber found the four former officials guilty of the war crimes of arbitrary detention against 385 individuals, cruel treatment against 49 individuals, torture against 303 individuals, and murder against 96 individuals.

title: Iran: Architects of crimes against humanity to suppress protests must face international justice to deter further massacres
content:
• New report finds Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity during their bloody suppression of the 2022 Woman Life Freedom uprising  
  • In-depth investigation exposes chain of command responsible for implementing state policy of lethal force to crush protests and identifies 87 officials who should be investigated for crimes against humanity  
  • Iranian authorities disproportionately targeted Kurdish and Baluchi communities with lethal repression and subjected them to the crime against humanity of persecution  
  • UN General Assembly should create an international criminal justice mechanism to tackle impunity for repeated mass protest killings culminating in January 2026 protest massacres

title: Why is Amnesty International calling for international justice for crimes against humanity in Iran?
content:
Content warning: This article contains descriptions of violence, including shootings, beatings, torture, sexual violence, and discrimination. It also mentions issues relating to suicide. We include these details to honour the victims and their families, who want the truth to be brought to light.

Protesters in Iran have been killed, tortured or imprisoned in the thousands for demanding their human rights and political change. The officials responsible for protest-related crimes against humanity are evading justice while survivors and relatives seeking justice are persecuted.

In late 2022, Iran was gripped by large-scale protests that became known as the Woman Life Freedom uprising. After years of painstaking investigations, Amnesty International has exposed how the Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity to crush the uprising. Based on its extensive documentation of the crimes committed and analysis of the security forces’ command structures, Amnesty International has identified 87 officials who must be criminally investigated for their role in these crimes.

title: Ecuador: Militarization Continues and the Armed Forces Still Refuse to Cooperate
content:
One year after the publication of the report “It was the military. I Saw Them“, which documented the enforced disappearance of 10 people from the Ecuadorian coast, including six children, in the context of President Daniel Noboa’s so-called “Plan Fenix”, some progress has been made. Nevertheless, the lack of cooperation by the Armed Forces in the criminal investigations and the deepening of the policy of militarization of the public security continue to be the main obstacles preventing all victims’ families from obtaining truth, justice, and reparation, and from ensuring the non-repetition of these crimes, Amnesty International said today. 

“The progress achieved over the past year demonstrates that it is possible to respond to the demands for truth and justice made by the families, civil society, and international mechanisms. Yet this progress remains insufficient as long as many of those families continue not knowing what happened to their loved ones and the military authorities continue to withhold essential information for the investigations,” said Ana Piquer, Regional Director for the Americas of Amnesty International.
